steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure with a box element
steps.instruction: Create a simple HTML file with a div element that has a class name 'box'
steps.hint: Start with a basic HTML structure and add a <div> element with class="box" inside the body.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Transition Basics</title>
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add a div with class="box" here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic HTML file ready for styling with CSS transitions.
successCriteria: The HTML file contains a div element with class="box" inside the body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the HTML structure with a box element. This gives us the foundation to apply CSS transitions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a div element with class="box" inside the body.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a simple HTML file with a div element that has class="box".

steps.title: Add basic styling to the box element
steps.instruction: Add a <style> block inside the <head> section to define CSS rules for the .box element. Style it with width: 200px, height: 200px, background-color: #3498db, and border: 2px solid #2980b9.
steps.hint: The <style> tag should be placed before the closing </head> tag. Use the selector .box to target the div element.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Transition Basics</title>
    <!-- Add a style block here -->
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add a div with class="box" here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will have a blue square appearance with a darker blue border when the CSS is applied.
successCriteria: A <style> block is added inside <head> containing CSS rules for .box with width, height, background-color, and border properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the basic styling for the box element. The CSS properties create a visible, styled square that we'll later animate.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but some required CSS properties might be missing. Make sure you've included width, height, background-color, and border for the .box selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styling isn't quite right. Remember to add a <style> block inside <head> and define CSS rules for .box with all four properties: width, height, background-color, and border.

steps.title: Introduce the transition property
steps.instruction: Add a transition property to the .box element in your style block, setting it to 'all 0.5s ease'.
steps.hint: The transition property should be placed inside the .box CSS rule, after the existing properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will have a transition property that will animate all property changes over 0.5 seconds with an easing effect.
successCriteria: The .box CSS rule includes a transition property with the value 'all 0.5s ease'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the transition property. This is the foundation for creating smooth animations when the box's properties change.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a transition property, but check the value format. It should be 'all 0.5s ease' to animate all properties over half a second with easing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The transition property wasn't added correctly. Make sure you add 'transition: all 0.5s ease;' inside the .box CSS rule.

steps.title: Add a hover state to trigger the transition
steps.instruction: Add a :hover pseudo-class to the .box element that changes its background color to a different color.
steps.hint: Create a new CSS rule that targets .box:hover and set a background-color property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The box will change color when hovered over, preparing to see the transition effect.
successCriteria: A .box:hover rule is added with a different background-color value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a hover state that will trigger the transition when the mouse moves over the box.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added a .box:hover rule with a background-color property.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a .box:hover selector and set a different background-color value inside it.

steps.title: Specify which property to transition
steps.instruction: Update the transition property in the .box rule to specify only the background-color property.
steps.hint: Replace the comment placeholder with 'transition: background-color 0.3s ease;' to target only the background color.
steps.expectedOutcome: The transition property is now set to only affect background-color changes.
successCriteria: The .box rule contains a transition property that specifies background-color with a duration and easing function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully specified that only the background-color property should transition.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the transition property includes 'background-color', a duration (like 0.3s), and an easing function (like ease).
steps.feedbackWrong: The transition property is missing or incorrect. It should target only the background-color property.

steps.title: Add a second property to transition
steps.instruction: In the .box hover rule, add a border-radius property to make the box round on hover, and update the transition property in .box to include both width and border-radius.
steps.hint: In the .box:hover selector, add border-radius: 50px;. Then, in the .box rule, change the transition property to transition: width 0.5s ease, border-radius 0.5s ease;.
steps.expectedOutcome: The box will smoothly transition both its width and border-radius when hovered over, becoming wider and rounded.
successCriteria: The .box:hover rule includes border-radius: 50px; and the .box transition property includes both width and border-radius with durations and easing functions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a second property to transition, making the box change shape smoothly on hover.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure both the hover state changes border-radius and the transition property includes both width and border-radius.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added border-radius to the hover state and updated the transition property to include both properties.

steps.title: Set different transition durations for each property
steps.instruction: In the .box rule, update the transition property to set a 0.5s duration for width and a 1s duration for background-color.
steps.hint: You can specify multiple transition values separated by commas. Each value should follow the pattern: property duration timing-function.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Example: different durations for different properties */
transition: width 0.3s ease, opacity 1s linear;
steps.expectedOutcome: The transition property in .box should have two values: one for width with 0.5s duration, and one for background-color with 1s duration.
successCriteria: The transition property includes both width 0.5s ease and background-color 1s ease.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set different durations for width and background-color transitions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both width and background-color have their own duration values in the transition property.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax: the transition property should list multiple values separated by commas, each with property, duration, and timing-function.

steps.title: Add a transition delay
steps.instruction: In the .box rule, add a 1-second delay to the transition property so the width change starts after a pause.
steps.hint: Add a delay value after the duration in the transition property, like 'transition: width 0.5s 1s ease;'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The box's width transition will now wait 1 second before starting when you hover over it.
successCriteria: The transition property in the .box rule includes a 1-second delay value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a transition delay. The width change will now pause for 1 second before animating.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a delay value (like '1s') to the transition property in the .box rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The transition property in the .box rule doesn't have a delay value. Add a delay (e.g., '1s') after the duration.

steps.title: Change the transition timing function
steps.instruction: In the .box rule, modify the transition property to include a timing function of ease-in-out for the width property.
steps.hint: Add ease-in-out after the duration in the transition property. The syntax is: transition: property duration timing-function;
steps.expectedOutcome: The box will now transition with an ease-in-out timing function, starting slow, accelerating in the middle, and slowing down at the end.
successCriteria: The transition property in the .box rule includes ease-in-out as the timing function for the width property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the ease-in-out timing function. This creates a smoother acceleration curve for the transition.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added 'ease-in-out' as the timing function in the transition property for the width.
steps.feedbackWrong: The transition timing function wasn't added correctly. Check that you've modified the transition property to include 'ease-in-out' after the duration.

steps.title: Use the shorthand transition property with all values
steps.instruction: Update the .box transition property to use the shorthand syntax with all four values: property, duration, timing-function, and delay.
steps.hint: The shorthand syntax is: transition: property duration timing-function delay; You'll need to include the border-radius property from the hover state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will have a single transition property that handles both width and border-radius changes with duration, timing function, and delay all specified in shorthand syntax.
successCriteria: The .box selector has a transition property using shorthand syntax with property, duration, timing-function, and delay values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used the shorthand transition property with all four values. This makes your CSS more concise and easier to read.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the shorthand syntax with all four values: property, duration, timing-function, and delay.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using the shorthand transition property with all four values. The syntax should be: transition: property duration timing-function delay;
